summary: Alexander Robertson worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (M.A. circa 1894–1898) and the University of Glasgow, and served as a missionary for the United Free Church of Scotland from 1902 to 1937.

Alexander Rogers worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College circa 1843–1845 and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2008, he earned a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh, studying under supervisors Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.

Alexander Schiller specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Appalachian State University, the University of California, San Diego, and Kansas State University (PhD 2025). In 2026, he is attested as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Alexander Studholme is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Between circa 1996 and 2000, he studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin.

Alexander W. Macdonald worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the CNRS (circa 1957–1989), the Musée de l'Homme (1972), Kailash (circa 1973), Paris Nanterre University (Professor circa 1973–1989), and the University of Paris (1982).
Alexander Walker worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of St Andrews and held a post at the East India Company from circa 1780 to 1812.

Alexander Wynne specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (DPhil 2000–2003). He was a Junior Research Fellow at St John's College, Oxford (2002–2006).

Alexander Yiannopoulos is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under numerous scholars, including supervisor Karin Myers, traditional teachers Sherab Sangpo and Khenpo Sherab Dorje, and teachers Georges B. J. Dreyfus and Tom Tillemans.

Alexander Zieseniss worked in Indology. He studied under Carl Bezold, Bruno Liebich, Ernst Leumann, and Walther Schubring across Heidelberg, Freiburg, Hamburg (PhD by 1928), Tübingen, and Berlin. He completed his Habilitation at Hamburg (1936–1941) and served as Privatdozent at Breslau (circa 1937–1945).

Alexander von Humboldt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at European University Viadrina, the University of Göttingen under Georg Forster and Christian Gottlob Heyne, Handelsakademie Hamburg, TU Bergakademie Freiberg, and the University of Jena, where he also held a post.

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen). He held positions at the universities of Leipzig (1995), Vienna (2001), and California, Berkeley (attested 2011–2026).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He studied at Tartu, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Saint Petersburg. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, Peking University, the Sino-Indian Institute, and the Harvard-Yenching Institute.

Alexandra David-Néel worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Paris and the Royal Conservatory of Brussels, and with Sylvain Lévi, Philippe Édouard Foucaux, Swami Bhaskarananda Saraswati, Kazi Dawa Samdup, and Lachen Gomchen Rinpoche.

Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, John de Vos, and Paul Y. Sondaar, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indology scholar who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as Professor of Rhetorics at Lycée Charlemagne, a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1835–1854), and an inspector for the Académie de Paris (circa 1838–1854).

Alexey Belyakov works in Buddhist and religious studies. After postgraduate study at Amur State University (2001–2010), he worked for the Amur Region Heritage Center (2007–2013), Amur State University (2013–2017), Heihe University (2017–2018), and Changchun University (2018).
Alexis Cordier was an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the École de santé navale circa 1890–1894 and earned a Dr.med. from the University of Bordeaux circa 1890–1894.

Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford and under Swami Lakshman Joo. His career at Oxford included posts at Merton, Brasenose, and All Souls colleges, as well as serving as Professor.

Alf Hiltebeitel was an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Haverford College and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner, he spent his career at George Washington University from 1968, becoming Columbian Professor in 1981.
